result.assumptions: linear elastic, small deflection, isotropic; faces clamped where fixed; no contact, preload or buckling
result.load_from: 30 g with the turret upside down (or the robot lifted by its turret): the panning group's 383 N lifts the 6810's outer race against the clamp (SendCutSend 6061-T6, 0.125 in), held by its 5 M3 screws (the load on the bore's edge, where the race bears)

excluded.why: elements touching a clamp or load patch: idealised supports make artificial spikes there; like the safety factor, the failure test leaves them out

overstressed_volume.definition: volume of the elements whose peak stress is past the strength (an upper bound), supports excluded, over the whole volume

assumptions: Linear elastic, small deflection, isotropic: printed parts use the weak (layer) direction strength. Every field scales with the load. It shows where and at what load the part first reaches its strength, not how a crack grows after that. Faces clamped where held; no contact, preload or buckling. Elements touching the clamp and load patches are left out of the failure test and capped at the design stress (their spikes are artefacts of the idealised supports). Stresses are element corner peaks, as the safety factor uses; the overstressed volume counts whole elements (an upper bound). The section cut shows the surface skin, not the stress inside.
